result.topic_en: Corollaries on representing a multiple of a prime of the form 4n+1 as a sum of two squares with roots less than 2n+1, counting such formulas and bounding the quotient, followed by the start of a scholium.
result.transcription:
114 RESIDVA EX DIVIS. POTESTATVM
cesse est; et cum neutrum per se diuisionem admittat, ea vtique ad $4n+1$ erunt prima.
Coroll. 1.
61. Euidens quoque est quadratum $xx$ infinitis modis accipi posse, cum omnia quadrata in hac forma $(m(4n+1)\pm x)^2$ idem residuum, quod $xx$ praebeant: vnde pro $x$ dabitur valor non solum minor quam $4n+1$, sed etiam minor eius semisse $\frac{4n+1}{2}$ seu minor quam $2n+1$.
Coroll. 2.
62. Semper ergo tales summae binorum quadratorum:
$1+pp,\ 4+qq,\ 9+rr,\ 16+ss,\ 25+tt$ etc.
exhiberi possunt, quae omnes sint per numerum primum $4n+1$ diuisibiles; atque ita vt singulorum radices sint minores quum $2n+1$.
Coroll. 3.
63. Cum multitudo numerorum minorum quam $2n+1$ sit $=2n$ ac semper bina quadrata disparia iungantur, multitudo harum formularum erit $n$: et quia talis summa binorum quadratorum minor est quam $2(2n+1)^2=8nn+8n+2$, quotus erit minor quam $2n+\frac{3}{2}$ seu $2n+2$.
Scholion.
64. Quo has summas binorum quadratorum pro quouis numero primo formae $4n+1$ facilius elice-

items.quote: Euidens quoque est quadratum $xx$ infinitis modis accipi posse, cum omnia quadrata in hac forma $(m(4n+1)\pm x)^2$ idem residuum, quod $xx$ praebeant: vnde pro $x$ dabitur valor non solum minor quam $4n+1$, sed etiam minor eius semisse $\frac{4n+1}{2}$ seu minor quam $2n+1$.
items.english: It is also evident that the square xx can be taken in infinitely many ways, since all squares of the form (m(4n+1) ± x)^2 give the same residue as xx; hence a value of x can be found that is not only less than 4n+1 but even less than its half (4n+1)/2, i.e. less than 2n+1.

items.quote:
Semper ergo tales summae binorum quadratorum:
$1+pp,\ 4+qq,\ 9+rr,\ 16+ss,\ 25+tt$ etc.
exhiberi possunt, quae omnes sint per numerum primum $4n+1$ diuisibiles; atque ita vt singulorum radices sint minores quum $2n+1$.
items.english: Therefore such sums of two squares 1+pp, 4+qq, 9+rr, 16+ss, 25+tt etc. can always be exhibited which are all divisible by the prime 4n+1, and in such a way that the roots of each are less than 2n+1.

items.quote: multitudo harum formularum erit $n$: et quia talis summa binorum quadratorum minor est quam $2(2n+1)^2=8nn+8n+2$, quotus erit minor quam $2n+\frac{3}{2}$ seu $2n+2$.
items.english: The number of these formulas will be n; and since such a sum of two squares is less than 2(2n+1)^2 = 8nn+8n+2, the quotient will be less than 2n+3/2, i.e. 2n+2.
